extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / scientific readers (astronomers, navigators, anatomists, experimentalists) reading the Philosophical Transactions
extracted.subtask_description: Writing short observational/experimental reports in natural philosophy (astronomy, navigation, anatomy, natural history) that present measurements, instrumentation, methods, and interpreted results with attention to accuracy and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute the moon's true southing exactly (not from moon's age)
rubrics_metrics.description: The moon's southing should be calculated exactly rather than inferred from the moon's age or the epacts (the practice of 'getting the moon's age by the epacts' and allowing 48 minutes of time for every day's age is false and produces error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the almanac practice that derives southing from moon's age and a 48-minute allowance per day; compute the moon's true southing to reduce large errors in predicting high-water times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume a constant interval between moon-southing and high-water
rubrics_metrics.description: It is incorrect to make the time of high-water by 'adding 3 hours constantly' to the moon's southing; the interval between the moon's southing and high-water varies with lunar phase and other factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the simple rule 'add 3 hours' — the difference between southing and high-water changes (greatest nearer the neaps, least near highest springs). Tables must reflect this variability rather than a fixed offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate tide tables against many observations and quantify residuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Tide tables ought to be checked against many observed high-waters and corrected; a good agreement is when calculated times differ from observations by less than a quarter of an hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect numerous high-water observations (e.g., >60) at the relevant place (Tower-wharf/Greenwich), derive corrections, and aim for residuals typically under 15 minutes; acknowledge limits in measuring exact high-water times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide times for both high-waters and note environmental caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Tide tables should show the times of both high-waters (not only the one following moon-southing) and expressly note that exceptional conditions (drought, extreme frost, strong winds, great freshes) can make tides hold up longer or shorter than table times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both peaks where relevant and include clear caveats about meteorological/hydrological conditions that can systematically alter observed high-waters versus the table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide simple reduction method to adapt a tide-table to other ports
rubrics_metrics.description: A tide-table may be reduced/made to serve other ports by adding or subtracting a fixed time offset equal to the observed lead/lag of that port's high-water relative to the table's port.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the rule and mention that it relies on obtaining the observed difference for the other place; do not invent offsets from unverified mariners' accounts (their opinions differ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report instrumentation, observational method, and counting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports must state the instruments and methods used (e.g., quadrant radius, telescope, pendulum used as a seconds-beat, ropes, lines, candles, torches, speaking trumpet) and how timings/measurements were taken (counting pendulum vibrations, measuring depths by ropes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instrument size, construction (e.g., 'a pendulum of a string and a bullet 8Q inches long'), how observers synchronized/count, and any approximations made so readers can assess accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer strict calculation from observations for orbital/positional determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining cometary path, velocity, orbital angle, etc., present strict calculations rather than loose deductions from a consideration of the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a table or path is 'not composed from any accurate calculation' make that explicit and, when possible, follow through with rigorous computation; distinguish preliminary looser inferences from final calculated results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative positional/kinematic tables for astronomical objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and publish meridian altitudes, distances from fixed stars, daily motion in orbit, latitude of object, daily increase in motion, and other numerical data in tabular form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give dates/times, measured angles/longitudes/latitudes, and changes over intervals so others can reproduce or further calculate orbital elements; include comments on uncertainties (e.g., tail length varying, coma/nucleus appearance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document experimental procedure and physiological state in biological experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: In experiments (e.g., injecting indigo tincture into a dog's intestine to test chyle coloration) record details of procedure (amount injected, warming, location in gut, stitching, timings) and the physiological state of the subject (fed vs fasting) because results depend on these conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report controls and subject state (fasted 40 hours vs fed), volumes used (e.g., 'about 12 oz.'), timings before re-opening (e.g., 'after full 3 hours'), and any differences observed between conditions to allow interpretation of negative/positive results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require direct visual/empirical evidence for physiological claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about physiological pathways (e.g., 'the lacteal veins receive their contents from the cavity of the intestines') should be supported by direct visual evidence such as seeing colored chyle issuing from lacteal veins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer direct observation (cutting lacteals and observing colored chyle) over inference; describe what was seen and where (e.g., 'we plainly saw a thick blue chyle to issue forth').

rubrics_metrics.name: Use methodical measurement and repeated observation in field explorations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explorations (e.g., descent into Pen-park hole) should use ropes and tackling to measure depths and lengths, repeat visits/observations, measure dimensions (length, breadth, depth), and observe temporal behavior (checking for ebb and flow by staying through predicted cycles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record measured numbers (e.g., 'down the tunnel ... 39 yards', 'greatest length 75 yards', 'water 8 fathoms deep'), note repeated stays and durations (stayed 2 hours and 1), and test hypotheses (miner claimed ebb and flow but observation over cycles proved otherwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include diagrams/plots with labeled features for spatial clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: For cavities, geological profiles, or spatially complex features include a profile and ground-plot and label points (A, B, C, etc.) with explanations of what each letter denotes (e.g., A = superficies, B = lead-ore pit...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide figures with keyed labels and a legend so the narrative measurements and statements can be interpreted spatially; reference the figure in text ('see fig. 1, pi. 16').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record specimen provenance, precise morphological measures, and acknowledge sample-size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Anatomical descriptions should provide specimen origin, exact dimensions (length, girth), counts (number of scales, rows), and comparisons with related species; explicitly note that observations from a single subject cannot complete a species' history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the source (e.g., 'sent from Virginia'), exact measures ('4 feet 5 inches long', 'girth at middle 6½ inches'), counts ('from neck to anus we numbered 168'), and a caveat about representativeness ('the observations I shall give are such as a single subject would afford').

rubrics_metrics.name: For editorial/textual work: collate manuscripts, provide translations and notes, correct transcribers' mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: When editing ancient or previously imperfectly printed texts (e.g., Ptolemy's Harmonics), compare multiple manuscript copies to restore and perfect the text, supply a new translation, and add notes and an appendix discussing variant doctrines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligently compare codices (e.g., 'Ex Codd. Mss. Undecim'), rectify mistakes (especially in numbers), add Latin translation and explanatory notes, and append comparative discussions of the subject-matter for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: State uncertainties, observational limits, and qualify claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should explicitly state where data are preliminary, where calculations are omitted, and the limits of the observations/methods (e.g., 'it would be tedious to mention all these' or 'not composed from any accurate calculation' or 'would be desired but cannot be expected').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label provisional work as such, avoid overclaiming from single or rough inferences, and indicate what further calculation or repetition would be required to finalize conclusions.
